British Patent Data & Industrial Innovation Analysis

Academic Spatial & Temporal Visualizations (1700–1830)

British Patent Dynamic GIS Information System

Spatial Analysis & Methodology

  • Industrial Agglomeration: The interactive map illustrates pronounced spatial clustering across 18th-century Britain, with optical and precision instrument patents highly concentrated in Metropolitan London, contrasting with northern and midland manufacturing centers.
  • Data Integrity: Each marker integrates multi-tier geocoding accuracy levels alongside historical applicant metadata to ensure robust quantitative evaluation.

Spatial Distribution of 18th-Century British Patents

Spatial Distribution Interpretation

  • Core-Periphery Structure: Patent density demonstrates a clear core-periphery paradigm centered on London and extending along vital transportation and resource corridors in the Midlands.
  • Technological Specialization: Sector-specific clustering highlights regional comparative advantages, such as textile innovations clustering in Lancashire and Yorkshire.

Temporal Trend of Patent Activites (1700–1830)

Temporal Trend Interpretation

  • Take-off Phase: 5-year interval aggregation indicates steady baseline activity prior to 1760, followed by exponential growth through the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
  • Institutional & Technological Correlates: Surges align closely with landmark mechanical innovations and institutional adjustments during the Industrial Revolution.

Decadal Evolution of Patent Technical Categories

Categorical Evolution Interpretation

  • Phase Shifts: Textiles dominate patent volume peaks during the 1770s–1790s, while steam power and metallurgy expand substantially into the 19th century.
  • Industrial Transition: The cross-decadal matrix captures the transition of inventive activity from early mechanization toward heavy industrialization.
